new_statements.quote: 2.4 Stress. The primary stress falls on the last syllable of a phonological word. botani [bo̜ta'ni] 'stingray', ima [i'ma] 'story', shikata [tsʰika'ta] 'sour'. In (diachronically) complex words, the secondary stress falls on the last syllable of the first (historical) morpheme. hinomadini [hiˌnu̜madi'ni] 'daughter-in-law', hidobadi [hiˌdo̜ba'di] 'son-in-law'. [p. 28] ... [p. 5:] There are no contrastive suprasegmental features ... Stress is always word-final. [p. 46:] Since stress falls on the last syllable of a phonological word, enclitics are stressed, except when followed by another enclitic.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the saved Google Books preview page images of Dienst 2014, A Grammar of Kulina (MGL 66), under and read them directly. : section heading '2.4 Stress' followed by 'The primary stress falls on the last syllable of a phonological word.' with botani [bo̜ta'ni] 'stingray', ima [i'ma] 'story', shikata [tsʰika'ta] 'sour'; then 'In (diachronically) complex words, the secondary stress falls on the last syllable of the first (historical) morpheme.' with hinomadini [hiˌnu̜madi'ni] 'daughter-in-law', hidobadi [hiˌdo̜ba'di] 'son-in-law' -- all verbatim as quoted. continues: 'The secondary stress falls on the final syllable of the historical morpheme hino ~ hido 'grandchild' in both cases, althoug…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed and non-contrastive: primary stress falls on the final syllable of the phonological word (which includes enclitic postpositions/particles, so a single enclitic carries the stress; with stacked enclitics the last one does).
new_statements.secondary_stress: In diachronically complex (historically compound) words, secondary stress falls on the last syllable of the first historical morpheme, e.g. [hiˌnu̜madi'ni], [hiˌdo̜ba'di], regardless of how many syllables follow (pp. 28-29).
new_statements.exceptions: Portuguese loans with unassimilated stress and morpheme-final diphthongs, where stress is marked with an acute in the orthography (p. xix); enclitic information-structure markers attract the stress from a preceding postposition (p. 179 snippet); an enclitic followed by another enclitic is unstressed (p. 46).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word = grammatical word plus following monosyllabic enclitics (postpositions, particles); examples are citation forms of nouns/adjectives. Author states there are no contrastive suprasegmental features (p. 5).
new_statements.identity_note: Dienst 2014 describes Kulina (Madihá of the Kulina ethnic group, mainly upper Purus and Juruá, Brazil, with data also valid for Peruvian Kulina); he treats Kulina, Deni (deni1241) and Western Jamamadi as a Madihá dialect continuum but the stress statement is for Kulina proper = culi1244. SIL 'Madija/Culina' works (Adams, Agnew, Boyer, Wright) describe the Peruvian Purus variety of the same language.
